HP:0003076.label: Glycosuria
HP:0003076.text: partial defect in renal glucose reabsorption

variants.omim_name: SLC5A1, SINGLE MISSENSE MUTATION IN SGLT1

records.label: Proband

phenotypes.text: absent intestinal glucose transport (jejunal mucosa unable to concentrate glucose)
partial defect in renal glucose reabsorption

records.segregation: Both parents and a half sister had intermediate impairment of glucose transport, consistent with heterozygosity; an asymptomatic brother had normal transport
quotes: investigated in a 3 yr old patient with congenital glucose-galactose malabsorption, her family, and 16 normal volunteers
The proband's mucosa was unable to concentrate glucose throughout a 60 min incubation period.
A partial defect in renal glucose reabsorption was found in the proband.

records.label: Oriental-Iraqui Jewish family
quotes: Glucose-galactose malabsorption in an Oriental-Iraqui Jewish family.

records.label: GGM family
quotes: We have now amplified SGLT1 complementary DNA and genomic DNA from members of a family affected with GGM by the polymerase chain reaction.
Sequence analysis of the amplified products has revealed a single missense mutation in SGLT1 which cosegregates with the GGM phenotype

records.label: 30 new GGM patients
quotes: The gene has now been screened in 30 new patients, and a heterologous expression system has been used to link the mutations to the phenotype.
The phenotype is neonatal onset of diarrhea that results in death unless these sugars are removed from the diet.

records.label: Two proband siblings
records.segregation: One sib fetus was heterozygous and one cousin fetus was not a carrier; both were unaffected at age 2 years
quotes: Two proband siblings with GGM were previously demonstrated to contain a missense mutation (D28N) in the Na(+)-dependent glucose/galactose cotransporter (SGLT1) that accounts for the defect in sugar absorption.
Prenatal screening for GGM was performed in two subsequent pregnancies in this large consanguineous family.

records.label: Eight Arab children with GGM
records.ancestry: Arab (6 Saudi Arab, 2 other Arab nationalities)
quotes: Eight children with chronic diarrhea from glucose-galactose malabsorption from eight different families are presented. Six children are Saudi Arabs and two are of the other Arab nationalities.
They were first seen for chronic watery diarrhea, present since birth, and failure to thrive.
One child had a renal stone at the first visit, and another was discovered to have one on follow-up.

records.label: 33 GGM patients from a large Old Order Amish pedigree
records.segregation: The variants co-segregated with the GGM phenotype in all affected individuals
quotes: Here, we report 33 patients with GGM from a large Old Order Amish pedigree and the associated mutations in SLC5A1 gene. Clinically, all affected individuals presented with classic watery diarrhea and dehydration.
The increased bowel sounds, distended abdomen, vigorous nursing regardless of their illness, and irritability and apathy were also noted as part of the initial presentation.

revealed four homozygous missense mutations, c.152A>G (p.N51S), c.1231G>A (p.A411T), c.1673G>A (p.R558H), and c.1845C>G (p.H615Q), that co-segregate with the GGM phenotype in all of the affected individuals.

notes.statement: Xin and Wang (2011) reported that when patients were diagnosed correctly and managed adequately, the diarrhea stopped at once and they rehydrated quickly, and normal growth and development followed. When the disease was not recognized, the clinical course was prolonged.
quotes: Patients underwent a dramatic turnaround with an immediate cease of the diarrhea and a quick rehydration if they were correctly diagnosed and adequately managed, followed by a normal growth and development pattern afterwards; whereas a prolonged clinical course would follow if the disease was not recognized.

notes.statement: Xin and Wang (2011) suggested that the SLC5A1 mutations associated with GGM in the Amish reflect a founder effect. They concluded that population-specific genetic testing is needed to make the early diagnosis that is critical for a favorable outcome.
quotes: These findings suggest that founder effect of the SLC5A1 mutations associated with the disease in Amish and a population specific genetic testing is in need to pursue an early diagnosis which is critical for a favorable outcome.

notes.statement: ANDERSON et al. (1965) reported an inborn defect of intestinal absorption of certain monosaccharides.
quotes: AN INBORN DEFECT OF INTESTINAL ABSORPTION OF CERTAIN MONOSACCHARIDES.

notes.statement: Abdullah et al. (1996) reported that all 8 Arab children with glucose-galactose malabsorption responded clinically to a fructose-based formula and were thriving at follow-up.
quotes: All the children responded clinically to fructose-based formula, and they are thriving at follow-up.

notes.statement: Abdullah et al. (1996) confirmed the diagnosis of glucose-galactose malabsorption by laboratory investigations including small-bowel biopsy, histology, and small-bowel enzyme assay; mean age at presentation was 10.6 months.
quotes: Laboratory investigations, including small-bowel biopsy, histology, and small-bowel enzyme assay, confirmed the diagnosis of glucose-galactose malabsorption.
The mean age of the children at the time of presentation was 10.6 months.

notes.statement: Martín et al. (1996) carried out prenatal screening in 2 pregnancies in a consanguineous GGM family. They PCR-amplified exon 1 of SGLT1 and tested for the D28N mutation by EcoRV restriction digestion. The proband's sib was heterozygous and a cousin was not a carrier, and both children were healthy without diarrhea at 2 years of age.
quotes: The first exon of the SGLT1 gene was PCR-amplified from genomic DNA and screened for the presence of the D28N mutation by EcoRV restriction digestion.
The proband's sibling was heterozygous and a cousin was not a carrier of the D28N mutation. Both children at 2-years of age remain healthy and have had no diarrhoeal symptoms.

notes.statement: Martín et al. (1996) described glucose-galactose malabsorption as an autosomal recessive disorder that presents with severe osmotic diarrhea shortly after birth.
quotes: Glucose-galactose malabsorption (GGM) is an autosomal recessive disorder which presents with severe osmotic diarrhoea shortly after birth.

notes.statement: Martín et al. (1996) described glucose-galactose malabsorption as caused by a defect in the intestinal Na+/glucose cotransporter SGLT1. Diarrhea begins in the newborn period and leads to death unless glucose and galactose are removed from the diet.
quotes: Glucose-Galactose Malabsorption (GGM) is caused by a defect in SGLT1. The phenotype is neonatal onset of diarrhea that results in death unless these sugars are removed from the diet.

notes.statement: Martín et al. (1996) screened the SGLT1 gene in 30 new patients with glucose-galactose malabsorption. They used a heterologous expression system to link the mutations to the phenotype, and found that defects in SGLT1 trafficking and function caused the disorder.
quotes: The gene has now been screened in 30 new patients, and a heterologous expression system has been used to link the mutations to the phenotype.
Defects in Na+/glucose cotransporter (SGLT1) trafficking and function cause glucose-galactose malabsorption.

notes.statement: Turk et al. (1993) used fluorescence in situ hybridization with a cosmid probe to refine the location of the SGLT1 gene, mutated in glucose/galactose malabsorption, to chromosome 22q13.1. The gene had previously been assigned to 22q11.2-qter.
quotes: The SGLT1 gene was previously shown to reside on the distal q arm of chromosome 22 (11.2-->qter). We have used a cosmid probe for fluorescence in situ hybridization, which refines the localization to 22q13.1

notes.statement: Turk et al. (1993) noted that, in two patients with autosomal recessive glucose/galactose malabsorption, the cause was a missense mutation in SGLT1. In vitro, the resulting asp28-to-asn change abolished SGLT1 transport activity.
quotes: In two patients with the autosomal recessive disease glucose/galactose malabsorption, the underlying cause was found to be a missense mutation in SGLT1, and the Asp28-->Asn change was demonstrated in vitro to eliminate SGLT1 transport activity.

notes.statement: Meeuwisse (1970) studied renal glucosuria in patients with glucose-galactose malabsorption.
quotes: Glucose-galactose malabsorption. Studies on renal glucosuria.

notes.statement: Elsas et al. (1970) concluded that familial glucose-galactose malabsorption is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. Both parents and a half sister of an affected girl had glucose transport values between those of normal controls and those of the proband.
quotes: We conclude that familial glucose-galactose malabsorption is inherited as an autosomal recessive trait
Both of her parents and a half sister demonstrated impaired glucose transport. Their values fell between normal and those of the proband.

notes.statement: Elsas et al. (1970) found impaired glucose influx in the jejunal mucosa of 3 heterozygotes, while glucose efflux was the same as in normal controls. Kinetic analysis showed reduced transport capacity (Vmax) with normal affinity (Km), suggesting that heterozygotes can be detected.
quotes: Influx of glucose was impaired but efflux of glucose from the mucosa of these three heterozygotes was identical with that in three normal controls.
A kinetic analysis indicated a reduced capacity (V(max)), but a normal affinity (K(m)) for glucose transport by their intestinal mucosa.

notes.statement: Elsas et al. (1970) showed that glucose transport by normal human jejunal mucosa was concentrative, saturable, and dependent on sodium and energy, and that it showed competitive inhibition. Absent intestinal glucose transport in the proband was accompanied by partial impairment of renal glucose transport. Fructose accumulation was similar in all subjects.
quotes: Glucose transport by normal human jejunal mucosa was concentrative, saturable, sodium and energy dependent, and exhibited competitive inhibition.
absent intestinal glucose transport is accompanied by partial impairment of renal glucose transport
All subjects accumulated fructose similarly.

notes.statement: Elsas and Lambe (1973) reported familial glucose-galactose malabsorption in which the glucose intolerance went into remission.
quotes: Familial glucose-galactose malabsorption: remission of glucose intolerance.

notes.statement: Turk et al. (1991) described glucose/galactose malabsorption as an autosomal recessive disease that appears within the first weeks of life. It is characterized by a selective failure to absorb dietary glucose and galactose from the intestine, which leads to severe diarrhea and dehydration that are usually fatal unless these sugars are removed from the diet.
quotes: Glucose/galactose malabsorption (GGM) is an autosomal recessive disease manifesting within the first weeks of life and characterized by a selective failure to absorb dietary glucose and galactose from the intestine.
The consequent severe diarrhoea and dehydration are usually fatal unless these sugars are eliminated from the diet.

notes.statement: Turk et al. (1991) found a single missense mutation in the SGLT1 gene that cosegregated with GGM in an affected family. In Xenopus oocytes injected with the mutant cRNA, Na(+)-dependent glucose transport was completely lost.
quotes: Sequence analysis of the amplified products has revealed a single missense mutation in SGLT1 which cosegregates with the GGM phenotype and results in a complete loss of Na(+)-dependent glucose transport in Xenopus oocytes injected with this complementary RNA.
